answer: An economy resists sybils when identity is an opal, not a label: each agent earns distinct facets by completing verified work in unrelated domains—compute jobs, data checks, escrow mediation—each recorded on a ledger. One operator cannot cheaply fake all facets at once because each domain demands different scarce resources. Every facet is backed by a sable bond, a time-locked stake forfeited on proven fraud, so clones carry real cost. Trust grows like yarrow: new facets gain weight only after a maturation delay, so fresh identities stay low-weight while honest agents compound reputation.
